patches.value: F003 holds for arbitrary positive δ,ε. Discharge L2 to obtain existence of the stated arbitrarily fine arbitrarily cheap covers. Since q+1>0, N001, now for MaxProd(X), A×I and exponent q+1, implies H^(q+1)(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves the output proposition on the whole asserted domain without any positive-diameter assumption on the covering sets.

By the lower-infimum bound in N001, F004 implies C^s_δ(A)≤C^(s+1)_δ(A×I), including if no admissible product cover exists. This holds at every δ>0. Taking suprema over positive scales and using N001 for both positive exponents s and s+1 gives H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s and the scale. These are the complete scale and measure inequalities asserted in the output proposition.

Apply M008 to f_f and I, using the isometry in F003. It gives dimH(f_f '' I)=dimH(I)=1 by F002. Apply M006 to f_f '' I⊆F, also in F003, to get 1≤dimH(F)=T. Combining with F001 proves 0≤D≤n₀<∞ and 1≤T≤n₀+1<∞, together with dimH(I)=1 and the finite real identifications. The chosen point and its map do not occur in the output proposition.

Assume for contradiction L2: k_real>d_real+1. Put q_mid=(d_real+k_real-1)/2. Then d_real<q_mid<k_real-1, because k_real-1>d_real. F003 with q=q_mid gives k_real≤q_mid+1<k_real, a contradiction. Discharge L2 to obtain k_real≤d_real+1. Cast back by F001: T≤D+1. Finiteness is already supplied by N004. This proves the output proposition for every natural n₀, including zero.

F003 gives T≥D+1, and N005 gives T≤D+1. Antisymmetry proves T=D+1. Both dimensions and their sum are finite by F001 and N004. When n₀=0, N004 forces D=0 and the fibre branch already supplies the lower bound; the upper proof also covered this case. This proves the output proposition. Compactness remains an original hypothesis in the global specification, although this replacement proof does not use it.

By F001, j(n₀) is an isometry. Its explicit inverse sends a vector v∈Rn(n₀+1) to the pair consisting of its first n₀ coordinates in Rn(n₀) and its last coordinate, regarded as an element of L2Prod(n₀) using euclideanLift n₀. Coordinate evaluation shows that both composites are the identity. Hence j(n₀) is bijective. By the definitions of F,G,euclideanLift and j, a point of j(n₀) '' (euclideanLift n₀ '' F) is precisely a concatenation of x∈E and t∈I; conversely every such concatenation arises this way. Thus this image equals G. Specializing F001 to p=euclideanLift n₀ (x,t) and z=euclideanLift n₀ (y,u) yields the squared-distance formula stated in the output proposition for every such x,y,t,u. For n₀=0 the inverse still extracts the last coordinate and the empty initial tuple; every step is unchanged.
